name: Morocco (Alaouite dynasty)
summary: The kingdom of Morocco under the Alaouite dynasty, which has ruled since the 1630s–1660s. It was a French and Spanish protectorate from 1912 to 1956.

knownFor.label: Meknes under Moulay Ismail
knownFor.note: A walled imperial city built by Moulay Ismail.

knownFor.label: Tagine
knownFor.note: Slow-cooked stew in a cone-lidded pot.

location.value: North-west Africa, on the Atlantic and Mediterranean.

terrain.value: The Atlas Mountains run down the country’s backbone, with the Rif in the north and desert in the south.

climate.value: Mainly hot-summer Mediterranean and hot desert climates.

resources.value: Phosphates (the largest reserves in the world), farmland, fish.

disasters.value: A 6.8-magnitude earthquake near Marrakesh killed more than 2,800 people (2023).

migration.value: A large diaspora, especially in France (over one million Moroccans).

tradeRoutes.value: Trade with Europe across the Strait of Gibraltar.

wealth.value: A lower-middle-income country, with a growing economy based on farming, phosphates and manufacturing.

inequality.value: Large gaps between cities and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A semi-constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament; a reformed constitution was approved in 2011.

keyRulers.value: Moulay Rashid. Moulay Ismail (1672–1727). Mohammed V. Hassan II. Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: Hereditary in the Alawi dynasty; Hassan II was succeeded by his son in 1999.

institutions.value: The Makhzen (royal establishment) limits the powers of the elected parliament.

stability.value: The “Years of Lead”: repression under Hassan II from the early 1960s to the late 1980s.

eliteConflict.value: Rivalries within the elite and with tribes in earlier centuries.

armyAndTech.value: Moulay Ismail’s Black Guard army of enslaved soldiers.

majorWars.value: The Rif uprising (1921–26), the Sand War with Algeria (1963), and the Western Sahara war from 1975.

territoryChange.value: Annexed the former Spanish Sahara in 1975; it controls most of Western Sahara, a disputed territory.

alliancesRivals.value: Fought the Sand War with Algeria (1963); France and Spain are its main trade partners; the US backed its claim to Western Sahara (2020).

inventions.value: No major modern inventions; Morocco is known for the University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859.

scienceEducation.value: The University of al-Qarawiyyin, founded in Fez in 859, is considered by some, including UNESCO, the oldest university in the world.

openness.value: Open to trade with Europe, with the Strait of Gibraltar only 14 km away.

communicationTransport.value: Africa’s first high-speed railway, linking Tangier and Casablanca (2018).

religion.value: Sunni Islam; the king is “Commander of the Faithful”.

languageWriting.value: Arabic and Tamazight (official); French widely used.

artsArchitecture.value: Zellige, carved plaster, riads, gnawa music.

socialStructure.value: Arab and Amazigh (Berber) communities, with a monarchy at the centre of the state.

sharedIdentity.value: The monarchy and Islam are the main symbols uniting the country.

ideasReligions.value: Islam, practised by almost all Moroccans, with some Arab nationalism in the 20th century.

riseSignals.value: The Alaouites took Fez and Marrakesh in the 1660s.

peakPeriod.value: The long reign of Moulay Ismail (1672–1727), who built a strong army and unified the country.

declineSignals.value: European pressure in the 19th century, which led to the French and Spanish protectorates in 1912.

outcome.value: Morocco continues as an independent kingdom.
